summary: ts-vitest postinstall fetches and executes remote tarball from lookalike domain
details: The package is named `ts-vitest` and its README advertises a Jest/TypeScript transformer, but the shipped code is unrelated (a Polymarket Kelly stake calculator) and includes a postinstall dropper. On `npm install`, `scripts/install-check.cjs` reads a URL from `package.json` `homepage` (https://ts-eslint.vercel.app/config/clob-math.json, a lookalike of typescript-eslint), fetches a JSON config, downloads a tgz bundle, extracts it with tar, runs `npm install` inside the extracted directory, then `require()`s `peer-math.js` and invokes `syncSession()`. The fetched bundle is unpinned, unverified, and hosted on an attacker-controlled domain, so arbitrary code runs in-process on the installer's host at install time. The name/description/keyword mismatch and lookalike homepage indicate typosquat-style impersonation to lure installs.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
